subject.title: [Feature]: Make detached longwork final delivery ownership explicit

question: Which existing substrate should own the durable final-delivery obligation for detached or migrated longwork: subagent completion routing, pending-final delivery recovery, channel outbound delivery reports, or a narrower new owner-mode seam?
rationale: Current main has adjacent requester/session routing and pending-final recovery state, but the requested cross-surface single-owner policy changes model-facing/API behavior and message/session-state compatibility, so automation should not choose the public contract.

options.title: Extend subagent pending-final delivery
options.body: Use existing subagent run records and pending-final delivery state as the owner of the single-full-final obligation, adding the minimum owner-mode fields and proofs there.

options.title: Track in outbound delivery reports
options.body: Keep subagent routing mostly unchanged and make outbound delivery evidence own the durable obligation and retry/failure classification.

options.title: Move to a narrower follow-up issue
options.body: Defer this broad design thread only after a maintainer opens a more specific canonical issue naming the chosen owner substrate and proof requirements.

recommendation.title: Extend subagent pending-final delivery
recommendation.body: Use existing subagent run records and pending-final delivery state as the owner of the single-full-final obligation, adding the minimum owner-mode fields and proofs there.

likelyOwner.reason: The targeted history shows repeated adjacent subagent completion and final-delivery work, making this the strongest available routing signal for the product/API choice.
